name: NUST Entry Test (NET)
syllabus:
• Physics (30% - 60 MCQs): Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Modern Physics (FSc Part 1 & 2). Focus on numericals.
  • Mathematics/Biology (40% - 80 MCQs): Calculus, Algebra, Trigonometry. Heavy focus on Integration and Conic Sections.
  • Chemistry/CS (15% - 30 MCQs): Organic chemistry reactions or basic boolean algebra and networking for CS students.
  • English (10% - 20 MCQs): Synonyms, Antonyms, Prepositions, Reading Comprehension.
  • Intelligence (5% - 10 MCQs): Number series, coding-decoding, spatial reasoning.
timing:
• Total Time: 180 Minutes (3 Hours)
  • Total MCQs: 200
  • Negative Marking: None. Guess all unattempted questions in the last 5 minutes.
  • Format: Computer-Based Test (CBT) at Islamabad; Paper-Based at Quetta/Karachi.
tips:
1. Time Management: You have less than a minute per question. Do not get stuck on long Calculus problems.

2. Order of Attempt: Always attempt Intelligence and English first. Then do Chemistry/CS. Leave Math and Physics for the remaining 2.5 hours.

3. Best Resources: OETP books are the gold standard for NET. Practice their chapter-wise MCQs heavily.

name: National MDCAT (PMDC)
syllabus:
• Biology (34% - 68 MCQs): Cell structure, Biological molecules, Coordination, Genetics.
  • Chemistry (27% - 54 MCQs): Physical chemistry (moles, kinetics), Organic (hydrocarbons, alkanes).
  • Physics (27% - 54 MCQs): Force and motion, Work, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism.
  • English (9% - 18 MCQs): Vocabulary, grammar rules, sentence correction.
  • Logical Reasoning (3% - 6 MCQs): Critical thinking, letter/symbol series.
timing:
• Total Time: 210 Minutes (3.5 Hours)
  • Total MCQs: 200
  • Negative Marking: None.
  • Format: Paper-Based Test (PBT) conducted simultaneously across Pakistan.
tips:
1. Stick to the PMDC Syllabus: Do not study extra topics. The PMDC issues a strict syllabus outline every year.

2. Biology requires rote learning: Questions are often exact lines picked from the provincial textbooks. Memorize the tables and diagrams.

3. Physics shortcuts: Learn mental math for Physics. You are not allowed a calculator, so practice rounding off numbers (e.g., using 10 instead of 9.8 for gravity).

name: NUMS Entry Test
syllabus:
• Academics (150 MCQs): Biology (35%), Chemistry (25%), Physics (25%), English (10%).
  • Psychological Test (100 MCQs): Personality assessment, stress handling, ethics, and consistency questions. (5% weightage).
timing:
• Academic Test: 150 Minutes
  • Psychological Test: 30 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 250 (150 Academic + 100 Psych)
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Difficulty Level: NUMS is historically considered more straightforward than the National MDCAT. Questions are less tricky but require solid factual knowledge.

2. The Psych Test: Do not overthink the psychological part. They ask the same question phrased differently 4 times to check if you are lying. Be honest and consistent.

name: ECAT (UET Lahore)
syllabus:
• Mathematics (30% - 30 MCQs): FSc Math Part 1 and 2.
  • Physics (30% - 30 MCQs): FSc Physics Part 1 and 2.
  • Chemistry / CS / Stats (30% - 30 MCQs): Depending on your intermediate combination.
  • English (10% - 10 MCQs): Basic grammar and comprehension.
timing:
• Total Time: 100 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 100
  • Marking Scheme: +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect, 0 for unattempted.
tips:
1. Beware the Negative Marking: ECAT is dangerous because of the -1 deduction. DO NOT guess wildly. If you cannot eliminate at least two options, leave it blank.

2. Speed is everything: You have exactly 1 minute per question. Skip lengthy calculations immediately and come back to them if time permits.

name: FAST Nu-Test
syllabus:
• Advanced Math (50%): Calculus, Limits, Integration, Trigonometry, Matrices (FSc level).
  • Basic Math / IQ (20%): Ratios, percentages, algebra, age problems, basic geometry (Matric level).
  • Physics (10%) & English (20%): Basic concepts and grammar.
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 120
  • Negative Marking: -0.25 marks for every wrong answer.
tips:
1. Focus on Advanced Math: This section carries half the weight of the entire test. You cannot clear the FAST cutoff without scoring well here.

2. Basic Math is free points: Practice basic SAT/NTS quantitative questions. They are easy but tricky if you haven't practiced.

name: LUMS Admission Test (LCAT)
syllabus:
• Quantitative Section: Arithmetic, Algebra, Geometry, Data Analysis.
  • Verbal Section: Reading Comprehension, Evidence-Based Reading, Writing and Language.
  • Essay Section: A prompt requiring a structured, argumentative essay.
timing:
• Total Time: ~3 Hours (Similar to the SAT).
  • Format: Divided into timed sections. You cannot go back to previous sections.
tips:
1. LCAT vs SAT: LCAT closely mirrors the old Paper SAT. If you have been preparing for the SAT using Khan Academy or Erica Meltzer, you are fully prepared for LCAT.

2. The Essay Matters: LUMS values holistic admission. A well-structured essay demonstrating critical thinking can significantly boost your application.

name: USAT (HEC)
syllabus:
• Verbal Reasoning (35 Marks): Analogies, synonyms, sentence completion, comprehension.
  • Quantitative Reasoning (40 Marks): Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, equations, statistics.
  • Essay Writing (25 Marks): Write an essay (400-500 words) in either English or Urdu on a given topic. you should prepare.
timing:
• MCQ Section: 100 Minutes (75 MCQs)
  • Essay Section: 40 Minutes
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Treat it as a universal backup: USAT is now accepted by many newer and public sector universities across Pakistan as a standard entry test.

2. Write in your strongest language: You have the option to write the essay in Urdu. If your English expression is weak, an excellent Urdu essay will score much higher.

name: NTS NAT (National Aptitude Test)
syllabus:
• Verbal (20 MCQs): English grammar, sentence completion.
  • Quantitative (20 MCQs): Basic math, word problems, series.
  • Analytical (20 MCQs): Logic games, deduction puzzles, scenario analysis.
  • Subject (30 MCQs): E.g., NAT-IE (Pre-Eng), NAT-IM (Pre-Med), NAT-ICS.
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 90
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Master Analytical Reasoning: This is the section where most students fail. Buy a Dogar Brothers NTS book and practice drawing grids for logic games.

2. Give multiple attempts: NTS is held every month, and universities accept your highest valid score. Give it early and often.

name: Aga Khan University (AKU) Test
syllabus:
• Biology (20 MCQs): Conceptual application of FSc/A-Level bio.
  • Chemistry (20 MCQs) & Physics (20 MCQs): High-level problem solving.
  • Math & Science Reasoning (40 MCQs): Reading data, charts, graphs, and concluding scientific results.
timing:
• Total Time: 150 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 100
  • Negative Marking: Applies (-0.25).
tips:
1. Do NOT Rote Memorize: AKU does not ask straight textbook definitions. They will give you a scenario (e.g., a patient with X symptoms) and ask you to deduce the biological mechanism.

2. Practice SAT Science: The Science Reasoning section is very similar to the ACT Science section. Practice interpreting graphs and tables.

name: IBA Karachi Aptitude Test
syllabus:
• English / Verbal: Extremely high-level vocabulary, reading comprehension, error identification.
  • Mathematics / Quantitative: Algebra, Geometry, Word Problems, Arithmetic.
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Format: Separate strict cutoffs for Math and English.
tips:
1. The Cutoff Trap: You MUST clear the minimum cutoff in BOTH English and Math individually. Scoring 100% in Math but failing English means rejection.

2. Vocabulary is King: IBA English is notoriously difficult. Start memorizing SAT vocabulary words (Barron's 333) months in advance.

name: PUCIT Entry Test
syllabus:
• Mathematics (35 MCQs): Matrices, Integration, Conics.
  • Physics / CS / Stat (20 MCQs): Based on your FSc background.
  • English / Basic Math (15 MCQs): Quantitative logic and grammar.
timing:
• Total Time: 60 Minutes (Very fast-paced)
  • Total MCQs: 70
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips: 1. Speed over Depth: The PUCIT test is incredibly fast. The questions are relatively easy, but you have less than a minute per question. Do the easy ones first and guess the rest.

name: GIKI Admission Test
syllabus:
• Mathematics (30 MCQs): FSc Part 1 & 2 Math.
  • Physics (30 MCQs): Deep conceptual numericals.
  • English (20 MCQs): Comprehension and grammar.
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 80
  • Negative Marking: -1 for incorrect. +3 for correct.
tips:
1. Lengthy Numericals: GIKI Physics questions often require 2-3 step calculations. Do not waste time on a single question.

2. Math Dominance: Math and Physics carry equal weight, but Math is usually easier to score in if you know your formulas well.

name: PIEAS Admission Test
syllabus:
• Mathematics (30 MCQs)
  • Physics (30 MCQs)
  • Chemistry / CS (30 MCQs)
  • English (10 MCQs)
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 100
  • Negative Marking: -1 for incorrect. +3 for correct.
tips:
1. Conceptual Depth: PIEAS is known for highly conceptual physics and chemistry questions. Rote learning will not work here.

2. Strategic Guessing: Because of the severe negative marking, only guess if you can eliminate at least two options.

name: ETEA (KPK Medical/Engineering)
syllabus:
• Biology/Math (60 MCQs)
  • Physics (60 MCQs)
  • Chemistry/CS (60 MCQs)
  • English (20 MCQs)
timing:
• Total Time: 150 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 200
  • Negative Marking: None (historically changed, always verify current year rules).
tips:
1. KPK Board Textbooks: Do not rely entirely on Federal books. ETEA extracts direct lines from the KPK textbook board.

2. Time Pressure: 200 MCQs in 150 minutes means you must be rapid-fire with Biology and Chemistry to save time for Physics numericals.

name: NED University Entry Test
syllabus:
• Mathematics/Biology (25 MCQs)
  • Physics (25 MCQs)
  • Chemistry/CS (25 MCQs)
  • English (25 MCQs)
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 100
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Balanced Approach: NED gives equal weightage to all 4 subjects. Do not ignore English and Chemistry, as they can easily boost your overall aggregate.

2. Sindh Textbooks: Ensure you have reviewed the Sindh board curriculum thoroughly.

name: MUET (Mehran UET) Test
syllabus:
• Mathematics (30 MCQs)
  • Physics (30 MCQs)
  • Chemistry (30 MCQs)
  • English (10 MCQs)
timing:
• Total Time: 100 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 100
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Focus on Fundamentals: Questions are usually straightforward applications of textbook formulas.

2. Past Papers: Solve the last 5 years of MUET past papers, as concepts and even specific questions tend to repeat.

name: COMSATS Entry Test (NTS)
syllabus:
• Follows standard NTS NAT patterns (NAT-IE, NAT-ICS, NAT-IM).
  • Verbal, Quantitative, Analytical, Subject modules.
timing:
• Total Time: 120 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 90
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Give it early: COMSATS relies heavily on the NTS NAT score for its merit aggregate. Since you can take NAT multiple times, start in January and keep taking it to maximize your score.

2. Analytical Section: Buy a dedicated NTS prep book and practice the logic puzzles.

name: Dow University (DUHS) Test
syllabus: • Follows the standard PMDC MDCAT structure (Bio, Chem, Phy, Eng, Logic).
timing:
• Total Time: 210 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 200
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Tricky Phrasing: Historically, DUHS sets slightly more complexly phrased questions compared to UHS. Read the "EXCEPT" and "NOT" keywords carefully in questions.

2. Provincial Bias: Make sure you are thoroughly familiar with the Sindh Textbook Board diagrams and terminologies.

name: Sindh MCAT (JSMU)
syllabus: • Follows the standard PMDC MDCAT structure.
timing:
• Total Time: 210 Minutes
  • Total MCQs: 200
  • Negative Marking: None.
tips:
1. Time Management: Allocate no more than 40 seconds per Biology/Chemistry MCQ so you have 1.5+ minutes for each Physics numerical.

2. Memorization: Sindh board books contain specific numerical values and dates (especially in Biology). Memorize these.

name: Digital SAT
syllabus:
• Reading and Writing: Information and Ideas, Craft and Structure, Expression of Ideas, Standard English Conventions.
  • Math: Algebra, Advanced Math, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, Geometry and Trigonometry.
timing:
• Total Time: 2 hours and 14 minutes.
  • Format: Adaptive Digital Test (Bluebook app).
tips:
1. Adaptive Nature: The test has two modules per section. Doing well in Module 1 gives you a harder (but higher scoring) Module 2. Do not panic if Module 2 feels extremely difficult; it means you are in the high-score bracket.

2. Desmos is your friend: You have an inbuilt Desmos graphing calculator. Learn how to solve Algebra and System of Equations purely using Desmos to save massive amounts of time.
